root_cause.text: The driver conditionally skipped freeing RSS context VNICs in firmware when the interface was down (via the `netif_running()` check), causing VNIC resource leaks that led to failed RSS context restoration on subsequent interface open due to unmet VNIC reservations.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states: "Having that condition will make the driver leak VNICs in FW whenever close() happens with active RSS contexts. On the subsequent open(), as part of RSS context restoration, we will end up trying to create extra VNICs for which we did not make any reservation. FW can fail this request, thereby making us lose active RSS contexts." The patch diff removes the `if (netif_running(bp->dev))` wrapper from `bnxt_del_one_rss_ctx()`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove the netif_running() check so that VNIC and RSS context resources are always freed when an RSS context is deleted, preventing resource leaks when the device is down.
intent_record.what: Removed the conditional `if (netif_running(bp->dev))` that guarded the calls to `bnxt_hwrm_vnic_free_one` and the loop freeing VNIC contexts, making these operations unconditional.
intent_record.how: Previously, VNIC and RSS context resources were only freed if the network device was running. Now they are freed regardless of the device state, ensuring proper cleanup even when the device is down.

grouping_result.intent: Remove the netif_running() check so that VNIC and RSS context resources are always freed when an RSS context is deleted, preventing resource leaks when the device is down.

relevance_review.reason: The group directly removes the netif_running() check that caused VNIC resource leaks when the interface was down, which is the exact vulnerability root cause described.

candidates.rationale: The netif_running() check causes the freeing of RSS context VNICs to be skipped when the interface is down, leading to VNIC resource leaks and subsequent failures on interface reopen.
This VNIC freeing operation is only executed when netif_running() is true, so when the interface is down the VNIC resource is not freed, causing a leak.
This RSS context freeing call inside the loop is conditional on netif_running(), so it is skipped when the interface is down, leading to resource leaks that prevent proper RSS context restoration.
